evidence: CDIAL 8201 subsection 6 *pilīla explicitly gives Kalasha pilīlyak, Palula pilīlu and Bashkarik pilīl; Shina has ph- in the same branch. Selected long pilil forms retain that diagnostic repeated-l stem, with aspiration, vowel length and endings qualified. Turner warns of taboo variation and imperfect grouping across the overall family; local transmission remains unresolved.

CDIAL 8201 subsection 2 *piphīla explicitly gives Lahnda pehlā/pehlī and Awankari pèlā/pèlī ant. Awankari/Pothwari pel/pil forms match this regional family; vowel and aspiration variation are retained and qualified. This follows the western comparison rather than assigning short pil forms everywhere to *pilīla. Exact local transmission remains unresolved.

CDIAL 8201 subsection 5 *pippīḍa explicitly gives Bengali pipiṛā, Assamese piparā and Hindi pipṛā ant. Eastern pipra/pepura forms match the labial-plus-r branch with contraction, vowels and deaspiration qualified; the isolated Bengali pipʼa records an apparent reduced rhotic and is not corrected. The entry warns of taboo variation and uncertain deeper origin; local transmission is unresolved.

CDIAL 8201 first branch explicitly connects Nepali kamilo ant with dissimilated kipillaka/kiulī comparanda, preferring a *kãwilo history to karmin. Majhi/Bote kamila/kimila/komila preserve that ant family with vowels and endings qualified. Possible contamination with kīṭa/kṛmi and local transmission are not resolved.

CDIAL 3193 kīṭa explicitly includes Prakrit kīḍa/kīḍiyā worm/insect/ant and modern western kīṛī ant. The simple kiḍ/kiḍiyā responses fit this family with gender/number endings, vowels and retroflex notation retained. The semantic range includes ant; no source gloss is changed. Extra-v and extra-l forms are excluded pending morphology, and local transmission remains unresolved.
